old.bio: Eduardo is the Partner of DeForest’s Labor & Employment practice and one of the most respected voices in labor governance in Mexico. His background blends more than two decades advising multinational employers with senior public-sector experience, allowing him to translate complex regulatory environments into stable operational frameworks. He is known for structuring policies and documentation systems that support high-risk, labor-intensive operations, as well as for steering high-value disputes that require strategic judgement and procedural precision. His leadership extends across mandates involving litigation coordination, cross-state governance and preventive frameworks for clients such as Volkswagen, Cinemex, GeNi, Scheaffler, Benteler, SKF and Megacable.

new.bio: Javier is a technical specialist whose practice sits at the intersection of labor law, social security and regulatory compliance. His experience includes conducting complex audits, harmonising documentation across multi-plant structures and advising on labor components of acquisitions and restructurings. Known for his precise analytical approach, Javier is essential in mandates requiring meticulous documentation, accurate risk assessment and alignment with global corporate standards. His work is particularly relevant for industrial, infrastructure and advanced-manufacturing groups.

new.bio: Jaime brings the perspective of someone who has managed labor structures on a global scale. Before joining DeForest, he served as Legal Director for Mexico, Central and South America at ManpowerGroup, overseeing one of the largest employer workforces in the region. This experience shapes his approach to complex disputes, mass-litigation management, workforce transitions and collective bargaining negotiations in high-pressure environments. His influence extends into national policy circles through his role as Vice President of the labor, Social Security and HR Commission at CONCAMIN, reinforcing his standing as a reference point for employers navigating regulatory reform, cross-border HR structures and large-scale labor exposure.

Client: SCOTCH
Matter’s Value (specify currency) and/or other key numbers:
Matter Status (closed in last year or ongoing?):
		
			Matter’s Context:
SCOTCH engaged DeForest to review and restructure its corporate and labor framework following the introduction of Mexico's specialised services regime (REPSE). The matter required a multidisciplinary approach combining labor, corporate and regulatory expertise to ensure that the client's business model remained fully aligned with the country's evolving outsourcing framework.
		
		Firm’s role and main output:
Working jointly across its corporate and labor practices, DeForest carried out a comprehensive review of the client's corporate structure, specialised services model, bylaws and REPSE registration while simultaneously conducting an audit of more than eighty suppliers to determine the appropriate regulatory treatment of specialised services agreements.

The engagement demonstrates the firm's ability to advise clients on complex regulatory transformations where employment, corporate governance and commercial operations converge.

Matter’s Value (specify currency) and/or other key numbers:
Matter Status (closed in last year or ongoing?):
		
			Matter’s Context:
Grupo Solana, a diversified automotive and real estate group employing more than 1,200 people, retained DeForest to implement a complex employer substitution process affecting its workforce structure. The matter required careful coordination between labor and regulatory authorities to ensure business continuity while restructuring the group's employment platform.
		
		Firm’s role and main output:
DeForest designed and executed the legal strategy necessary to reactivate the employer registration that had previously been cancelled, allowing the employer substitution process to proceed without disrupting the client's operations. The firm coordinated the labor transition while ensuring full compliance with applicable employment regulations and preserving workforce stability throughout the restructuring.

The engagement illustrates the firm's ability to support complex corporate reorganisations where labor law plays a critical role in enabling business transformation.

Name of the Matter: | Confidential (Y/N):
Client: Poliuretanos Summa Woodbridge (PSW)
Matter’s Value (specify currency) and/or other key numbers:
Matter Status (closed in last year or ongoing?):
		
			Matter’s Context:
PSW engaged DeForest to design and implement a comprehensive restructuring affecting approximately eight companies operating across multiple Mexican states. The project required the separation of business functions, the redesign of the group's employment model and the creation of a specialised services platform aligned with Mexico's post-outsourcing regulatory framework.
		
		Firm’s role and main output:
DeForest developed the legal strategy supporting the group's restructuring, including the creation of a specialised services entity, employer substitution processes, the redesign of corporate purposes and the implementation of a workforce transition affecting multiple operating companies. In parallel, the firm represents the client in social security litigation before the Federal Court of Administrative Justice challenging tax assessments relating to two manufacturing facilities, while continuing to advise on broader labor and social security governance matters.

The engagement reflects the firm's ability to coordinate multidisciplinary projects where labor law, corporate restructuring and social security litigation converge to support large-scale business transformation.

new.bio: Andrés leads the firm’s practice in the Bajío region, one of Mexico’s most active industrial corridors. He is recognised for his ability to execute litigation strategies with speed, clarity and sensitivity to local dynamics—particularly in jurisdictions adapting to the post-reform judicial system. His work bridges the strategic frameworks designed by senior partners with the practical realities of implementation in critical regions. For many clients, Andrés provides the on-the-ground coordination that ensures consistency across the firm’s national approach.

new.bio: With nearly forty years at Volkswagen de México, including his tenure as General Legal Director, Raymundo embodies an uncommon depth of experience in corporate labor relations. He has played a central role in major regulatory transitions, high-stakes union negotiations and organisational restructurings that have defined the automotive sector in Mexico. His judgement is sought in matters where legal interpretation intersects with operational continuity and corporate strategy. His presence within the practice adds a level of senior insight that few labor teams in the country can access.
